cards.name: Black & White
cards.summary: Converts a colour image to monochrome (the document stays RGB) with six hue sliders, Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues and Magentas, that set how light each colour range turns in the grey result, so reds, skin or blue clothing can be pushed lighter or darker like a lens filter on black-and-white film. Tint turns the grey into a one-colour toned image (sepia, cyanotype).
use_for: black-and-white photo posters and editorial portraits with controlled tonal separation
dramatic red-filter mono looks: reds and skin light, blues and greens dark
sepia or toned vintage prints with Tint on
mono background plates behind colour type or a colour cut-out
avoid: a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Black & White (editable, maskable) instead of the destructive Image > Adjustments command

extreme slider values posterize and band smooth gradients; the scripted keys are NOT clamped (harvest probe: +-1,000,000 read back as sent), so keep to the dialog's slider range, which Adobe documents as -200..300 (not probed in this version)
a quick flat greyscale with no control: Desaturate (Ctrl+Shift+U) is one keystroke
the colour strip / flat colour areas of equal luminance can merge to the same grey: separate them with the hue sliders
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer (rasterize, or use the adjustment layer)

params.name: red
params.does: Lightness of red areas in the grey result (percent of the original): higher = reds and skin turn lighter, negative = near black
params.typical: 40 default; 80-150 for a red-filter look, -50..20 to darken reds

params.name: yellow
params.does: Lightness of yellows and warm beige / skin highlights
params.typical: 60 default; 80-150 brightens skin and warm walls

params.name: grain
params.does: Greens slider (charID 'Grn ', which reads back as stringID 'grain'): lightness of green foliage and green blocks

params.name: cyan
params.does: Lightness of cyan areas (sky, teal)

params.name: blue
params.does: Lightness of blue areas: negative values darken skies and blue clothes dramatically

params.name: magenta
params.does: Lightness of magenta / pink areas

params.name: useTint
params.does: Tint checkbox: colours the grey result with Tint Color (split by luminosity, like a toned print)
params.typical: off for pure mono, on for sepia / cyanotype

params.name: tintColor
params.does: Colour used when Tint is on

params.name: presetKind
params.does: Custom when the six values are passed; Factory with a preset file (Red Filter, Infrared, Maximum Black ...)

pairs_with: Levels or Curves after the conversion to set black and white points
Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Black & White with a mask to keep one element in colour
Filter grain / noise for a film-print feel
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("presetKind"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindType"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindCustom")); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("red"), 130); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("yellow"), 110); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("grain"), 40) /* Greens: key Grn = grain */; d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("cyan"), -10); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("blue"), -40); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("magenta"), 80); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("useTint"), false); /* tint: var c = new ActionDescriptor(); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("red"),225); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("grain"),211); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("blue"),179); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("tintColor"), stringIDToTypeID("RGBColor"), c); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("useTint"), true); */ executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("blackAndWhite"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Black & White (adjustmentLayer:blackAndWhite)
cards.cost: light: one pass over the layer, instant

review.changes: avoid: marked the -200..300 slider range as Adobe documentation, not harvested (the harvest only shows the keys are unclamped)

verified.note: Greyscale frame; red, orange and yellow blocks white, cyan and blue black, so the per-hue lens-filter mapping is visible.

cards.name: Brightness/Contrast
cards.summary: Two-slider tonal fix: Brightness lifts or lowers the overall tone and Contrast pushes tones apart or together. In the default (non-legacy) mode both work on a curve that protects highlights and shadows from clipping; Use Legacy shifts every pixel linearly and clips easily.
use_for: quick punch on a flat, washed-out photo or video frame
brightening a dark product shot before layout
lowering contrast for a faded, matte background plate behind text
avoid: precise tonal work or protecting a colour cast: use Levels or Curves
Use Legacy on photos: it clips highlights and shadows to flat white / black
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Brightness/Contrast

scripts: the harvest gives no defaults or ranges (keys declared in the terminology only, none read back); Adobe documents the dialog as Brightness -150..150 and Contrast -50..100 (legacy -100..100 each), not probed in this version: stay inside them
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: brightness
params.does: Overall lightness shift (midtone-weighted unless Use Legacy)

params.name: center
params.does: Contrast (the key is 'center', charID Cntr): positive spreads tones apart, negative flattens them

params.name: useLegacy
params.does: Old linear behaviour: shifts / stretches every pixel equally, clips easily

params.name: auto
params.does: Auto button: Photoshop picks brightness and contrast for the image

pairs_with: Vibrance or Hue/Saturation after a contrast boost to rebalance colour
Levels for setting exact black / white points first
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("brightness"), 35); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("center"), 80) /* Contrast */; d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("useLegacy"), false); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("brightnessEvent"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Brightness/Contrast (adjustmentLayer:brightnessEvent)

review.changes: avoid: marked the Brightness / Contrast ranges as Adobe documentation, not harvested; equivalents.CDR: Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity -> Effects/Adjust/Light (B/C/I is status hidden in CorelDRAW 2024, gone from the live Effects > Adjust menu; its own card sends new work to Light, whose Brightness and Contrast sliders do this job)

verified.note: Brighter with more contrast than the plate (ramp 63/127/191 to 61/172/236) without clipping the ends, as described.

cards.name: Channel Mixer
cards.summary: Rebuilds each output colour channel (Red, Green, Blue; Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black in a CMYK document) as a percentage mix of the source channels plus a constant, so colours can be swapped or shifted (e.g. blue foliage, infrared-style looks); with Monochromatic on it outputs one grey channel built from the chosen mix, a classic film-filter black-and-white.
use_for: custom black-and-white conversions mixed from the red, green and blue channels
surreal channel-swap colour looks (swap red and blue for alien skies or false-colour)
infrared-style foliage and colour-cast correction per channel
avoid: everyday colour correction: Color Balance, Curves or Hue/Saturation are easier to control
keep each output's total near 100 percent or the image brightens / darkens and clips
Monochromatic with no gray matrix renders solid black (the gallery frame before the matrix was sent): always send gray
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Channel Mixer
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: red
params.does: Output Red: channelMatrix object with source percentages (red / green / blue) and a constant; Adobe documents the dialog sliders as -200..200 (not harvested)

params.name: green
params.does: Output Green matrix

params.name: blue
params.does: Output Blue matrix

params.name: gray
params.does: Output Black (gray) matrix, used when Monochromatic is on
params.typical: red 40, green 40, blue 20 for a neutral mono

params.name: monochromatic
params.does: Monochrome checkbox: outputs a single grey channel from the gray matrix

params.name: presetKind
params.does: Custom for your own matrices; Factory presets include Black & White with Red / Orange / Yellow / Green / Blue Filter (RGB) and Black & White Infrared (RGB)

pairs_with: Curves or Levels after a monochrome mix to set contrast
Hue/Saturation to tame a channel-swap result
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("presetKind"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindType"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindCustom")); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("monochromatic"), true); var g = new ActionDescriptor(); g.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("red"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 60); g.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("grain"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 40); g.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("blue"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 0); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("gray"), stringIDToTypeID("channelMatrix"), g); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("channelMixer"), d, DialogModes.NO); /* colour swap instead: monochromatic false and put red / green / blue outputs, e.g. r.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("blue"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 100); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("red"), stringIDToTypeID("channelMatrix"), r). The output keys and the channelMatrix class are harvested, and so are its inner keys in Photoshop's terminology (red, green (= grain, same id 'Grn '), blue, cyan, magenta, yellowColor, black, constant), declared /integer, but percentUnit doubles are what Photoshop reads back and accepts: the gallery rendered gray 40 / 40 / 20 this way and the frame matched 0.4 R + 0.4 G + 0.2 B within 0.3 levels */
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Channel Mixer (adjustmentLayer:channelMixer)

review.changes: summary: added the CMYK outputs (cyan / magenta / yellowColor / black are harvested keys); params.red: marked -200..200 as Adobe documentation; scripting comment: the inner matrix keys are declared in the harvested terminology as /integer (the card said they were unharvested), recordings use percent doubles, putInteger fallback named

verified.note: Neutral black-and-white frame (all three channels equal everywhere) that matches 0.4 R + 0.4 G + 0.2 B of the plate within 0.3 levels: the colour bars become distinct greys (yellow lightest, blue darkest), the custom mono mix the card describes.

previous.note: Uniform black frame, the same cause as the adjustment layer: Monochromatic with no Gray weights. Proposed: a 40/40/20 Gray mix (keys from the channelMatrix class the adjustment-layer probe read back) in demo_proposed; blocked from demo_settings by the validator and the renderer, which cannot carry object values.

second_opinion.note: Re-checked: the frame is one colour (0/0/0), no plate or harness fault (the renderer's scripted route matched the dialogs pixel for pixel in the control); monochrome with no weights is the cause. The proposed matrices stay inside the harvested channelMatrix keys (red / grain / blue / constant, percent) and will show a clear change (red-blue swap on a warm photo; a 40/40/20 grey mix), but they need object support in validate_cards.py and the renderer before a rerender can use them.

cards.name: Color Balance
cards.summary: Shifts the colour cast separately in the shadows, midtones and highlights along three axes, Cyan-Red, Magenta-Green and Yellow-Blue, e.g. cool shadows with warm highlights for a teal-and-orange grade, or neutralising a yellow indoor cast. Preserve Luminosity keeps the tones from brightening or darkening.
use_for: warming or cooling a photo to match a brand palette
teal-and-orange or split-toned cinematic grades on posters and thumbnails
removing a colour cast from indoor or event footage stills
avoid: an empty descriptor fails (harvest: 'The parameters for command "Color Balance" are not currently valid'): pass the level lists explicitly; which of them are the minimum was not probed, the scripting call sends all three

+-40 in the shadows is already strong: in the gallery frame the dark greys went navy (grey 42 -> 0 / 3 / 56) and lost their red entirely although Preserve Luminosity was on; stay nearer +-20 on dark photos
precise neutral-point correction: Curves or Levels with the grey eyedropper are more exact
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Color Balance
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: shadowLevels
params.does: Shadows: list of 3 integers [Cyan(-)..Red(+), Magenta(-)..Green(+), Yellow(-)..Blue(+)] (order confirmed by the gallery frame: [-40, 0, 40] took red out of the shadows and added blue); Adobe documents each slider as -100..100

params.name: midtoneLevels
params.does: Midtones: same 3-integer list; the dialog's default tone range

params.name: highlightLevels
params.does: Highlights: same 3-integer list

params.name: preserveLuminosity
params.does: Keeps each pixel's luminosity so the shift changes colour only, not brightness

pairs_with: Curves for contrast before grading
Vibrance to control saturation after the shift
cards.scripting: function lv(c, m, y) { var l = new ActionList(); l.putInteger(c); l.putInteger(m); l.putInteger(y); return l; } var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putList(stringIDToTypeID("shadowLevels"), lv(-25, 0, 30)); d.putList(stringIDToTypeID("midtoneLevels"), lv(20, 0, -25)); d.putList(stringIDToTypeID("highlightLevels"), lv(20, 0, -30)); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("preserveLuminosity"), true); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("colorBalance"), d, DialogModes.NO); /* list type /integer /list is harvested; the order inside each list (cyan-red, magenta-green, yellow-blue) is confirmed by the gallery frame */
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Color Balance (adjustmentLayer:colorBalance)

review.changes: avoid: 'a script must pass all three level lists' was a guess (the harvest only shows the EMPTY descriptor fails), reworded; params.shadowLevels: marked -100..100 as Adobe documentation and the slider order as unprobed

verified.note: Clear split tone on the grey ramp: dark greys go blue-teal (42 -> 0 / 3 / 56, 79 -> 0 / 54 / 95), mid grey cools (127 -> 89 / 120 / 142), light greys go warm peach (212 -> 255 / 237 / 218); the colour bars saturate and the photo shadows turn navy while the wall stays warm: teal shadows with warm highlights as described. Same pixels as the adjustment-layer frame (difference 0.0).

previous.note: Render failed (gallery/ps_adjustment/failed.json): "General Photoshop error occurred ... The parameters for command "Color Balance" are not currently valid." The demo is the cause: it carries only preserveLuminosity, and Color Balance needs its three level lists (the harvest probe hit the same error). Proposed teal-and-orange level lists (three integers each, as harvested; no min/max was harvested, values kept within +-40) are in demo_proposed; they cannot go into demo_settings until validate_cards.py and the renderer accept list values.

second_opinion.note: Re-checked failed.json and the harvest probe (same "not currently valid" error with no level lists): the demo, not the effect or the plate, broke the render. Proposed lists are three integers each like the harvested defaults, moderate (+-40) and opposite in shadows and highlights, so they will read on the warm photo; blocked until list values are accepted by validate_cards.py and encoded by the renderer.

cards.name: Color Lookup
cards.summary: Remaps every colour through a lookup table: a 3D LUT file (.cube, .3dl, .look, .csp), an abstract profile or a device link profile, giving a one-step film or cinematic grade such as Bleach Bypass, TealOrangePlusContrast or a Fuji / Kodak film emulation. With no table chosen it does nothing, so it needs a LUT file as input.
use_for: one-click cinematic or film-stock grades on photos and video stills
matching a still to a LUT already used on the video edit
moody campaign looks (Moonlight, FoggyNight, Candlelight) across a set of images
avoid: no LUT chosen = no visible change: the harvest's params do not include a key that carries the table file or its data, so a scripted apply with chosen values is unproven; record one apply with ScriptListener and replay that descriptor
the 'Name' param is declared as /classStringFormat and its harvested enum (string / format / type format) are type codes, not LUT names
strong LUTs crush shadows and shift skin tones: lower the layer opacity (on the adjustment layer) instead of stacking
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Color Lookup
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: lookupType
params.does: Kind of table: 3D LUT file, abstract profile or device link profile

params.name: LUTFormat
params.does: File format of the 3D LUT (CUBE, 3DL, 3DLS, CSP)

params.name: dither
params.does: Adds slight noise to avoid banding in smooth gradients after the remap

params.name: dataOrder
params.does: Channel order of the LUT data (RGB or BGR)

params.name: tableOrder
params.does: Index order of the table (RGB or BGR)

cards.demo_input: needs a LUT from extra.lut_files, e.g. TealOrangePlusContrast.3DL (Presets/3DLUTs); without it the demo renders unchanged
pairs_with: Curves or Levels before the LUT to normalise exposure
Vibrance after a desaturating LUT
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("lookupType"), stringIDToTypeID("colorLookupType"), stringIDToTypeID("3DLUT")); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("LUTFormat"), stringIDToTypeID("LUTFormatType"), stringIDToTypeID("LUTFormat3DL")); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("dither"), true); /* + the LUT itself: not covered by the harvest (no file / data key probed); add the keys a ScriptListener recording of the dialog produces */ executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("colorLookup"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Color Lookup (adjustmentLayer:colorLookup)
cards.cost: light: instant once the table is loaded

verified.note: Untested: status needs_input (a LUT file is required and none is supplied), so the gallery skipped it (not_rendered.json).

second_opinion.note: No frame on disk and the id is listed in not_rendered.json / failed.json; the reason given matches the card status and the harvest.

cards.name: Curves
cards.summary: The most precise tonal and colour tool: a graph mapping input tones to output tones, on the composite or per channel. An S-curve adds contrast, lifting the black point gives a faded matte, per-channel curves build colour grades (cross process, split tone); factory presets include Increase Contrast (RGB), Strong Contrast (RGB), Cross Process (RGB) and Negative (RGB).
use_for: contrast S-curves and faded matte looks on photos
per-channel colour grading (cross-process, warm highlights / cool shadows)
exact black / white point and midtone corrections for print
avoid: steep curves posterize and band smooth skies and gradients
presetKind Custom with no 'adjustment' list is the identity curve (the gallery's first frame was unchanged): always send the points
transferFunction is a read-back integer whose role the harvest does not record (probe: values wrap modulo 256, 1000000 -> 64); leave it at 0
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Curves
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: adjustment
params.does: Curve definitions: per channel, a list of input/output points (0-255)

params.name: presetKind
params.does: Default (identity), Custom (your points) or Factory / User preset loaded from 'using'

params.name: using
params.does: Path of a preset (.acv) file to load
params.typical: a factory preset such as Cross Process (RGB)

pairs_with: Hue/Saturation or Vibrance after a contrast curve
Black & White before a toning curve
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("presetKind"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindType"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindCustom")); var ca = new ActionDescriptor(), ch = new ActionReference(); ch.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("channel"), stringIDToTypeID("channel"), stringIDToTypeID("composite")); ca.putReference(stringIDToTypeID("channel"), ch); var pts = new ActionList(), xy = [[0,0],[64,40],[192,220],[255,255]]; for (var i = 0; i < xy.length; i++) { var p = new ActionDescriptor(); p.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("horizontal"), xy[i][0]); p.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("vertical"), xy[i][1]); pts.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("paint"), p); } ca.putList(stringIDToTypeID("curve"), pts); var adj = new ActionList(); adj.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("curvesAdjustment"), ca); d.putList(stringIDToTypeID("adjustment"), adj); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("curves"), d, DialogModes.NO); /* the key adjustment, class curvesAdjustment and its keys channel (/channelReference) and curve (/point list), and point.horizontal / vertical (floats) are declared in the harvested terminology; 'paint' is the stringID Photoshop reads back for the point class 'Pnt '. the gallery rendered this structure (an S-curve; the tones landed on the points within 1 level) */
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Curves (adjustmentLayer:curves)

review.changes: summary: preset names made exact (harvested as '... (RGB)'); scripting comment: the curve / point keys are declared in the harvested terminology, not only in ScriptListener lore

verified.note: S-curve contrast that lands on the sent points: plate tone 64 -> 40, 128 -> 128, 192 -> 215 (40 -> 21, 215 -> 234), so shadows deepen and highlights brighten while mid grey holds; colours gain punch, no colour shift on the grey ramp. Same pixels as the adjustment-layer frame (difference 0.0).

previous.note: Untested: frame identical to the plate (diff 0.0): presetKind custom with no curve points is the identity curve; points need the unharvested Adjustment object, which the renderer cannot encode.

second_opinion.note: Frame vs ref diff 0.0 confirmed in index.json: nothing was applied, so the effect is untested rather than broken; the card text is not contradicted by the frame.

cards.name: Desaturate
cards.summary: Removes all colour in one step, setting saturation to zero while the document stays RGB; there are no settings, so the grey result is flat and every colour of equal lightness turns the same grey.
use_for: fast grey placeholder or background plate behind colour type
removing colour from a selection to leave a spot-colour element
a neutral base before toning with Gradient Map or a colour fill
avoid: controlled black-and-white conversions: use Black & White or Channel Mixer (Monochromatic)
different colours of similar lightness (the colour-strip blocks, red and green) merge into one grey and lose separation
a non-destructive edit: there is no Desaturate adjustment layer; use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Hue/Saturation with saturation -100 or Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Black & White
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer
pairs_with: Levels or Curves to add contrast to the flat grey
Gradient Map for toning the grey result
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer at saturation -100 (no Desaturate adjustment layer exists)

verified.note: Flat greyscale; orange and yellow blocks land on the same grey (127), showing that colours of equal (max+min)/2 lightness merge, as the card says.

cards.name: Equalize
cards.summary: Redistributes the image's brightness values so they spread evenly across the full range, the darkest pixel becoming black and the brightest white: a flat, low-contrast image turns harsh and high-contrast, often with colour shifts, blown areas and noisy banding. With a selection it can equalize only the selected area or the whole image based on the selection.
use_for: revealing hidden detail in a very flat or dark image (diagnostic)
deliberately harsh, gritty, over-processed poster looks
a quick starting point before a gentler Levels pass
avoid: a natural correction: it ignores the image's intent and usually overdoes contrast; use Levels, Curves or Image > Auto Tone
smooth gradients and skies band and get noisy

the mapping of the area values to the dialog's two options is not recorded in the harvest; selectionEnum is presumably 'Equalize Selected Area Only' and image 'Equalize Entire Image Based on Selected Area'
no adjustment layer exists for it; work on a duplicate layer to keep the original
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: area
params.does: With an active selection: equalize only the selection, or the whole image using the selection's histogram; with no selection the whole image is equalized

pairs_with: Fade-style blending: put it on a duplicate layer and lower the opacity
Hue/Saturation to tame the colour shifts it causes
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("area"), stringIDToTypeID("areaSelector"), stringIDToTypeID("image")); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("equalize"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no: rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and has no adjustment-layer version; apply it to a duplicate layer

verified.note: Brighter, contrast-stretched frame with the midtones lifted (ramp 63/127/191 to 84/168/232) and the light wall near white; this plate already spans black to white, so the harsh look the card predicts for flat images is milder here.

cards.name: Exposure
cards.summary: Photographic exposure control: Exposure brightens or darkens in stops (mostly the highlights), Offset lifts or crushes the shadows and midtones with little effect on highlights, and Gamma Correction bends the midtones. Designed for HDR / 32-bit images but works on 8 and 16 bit; factory presets are Plus / Minus 1.0 and 2.0.
use_for: fixing under- or over-exposed photos by stops
bright high-key, blown-out looks for fashion or minimal posters
crushed or lifted blacks for a moody or faded grade (Offset)
avoid: large positive Exposure on 8-bit images clips highlights to flat white with no recovery
general contrast shaping: Curves or Levels give finer control
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Exposure
'gamma' is declared in the terminology but not read back; the dialog's slider is gammaCorrection
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: exposure
params.does: Exposure in stops (-20..20): positive brightens, mostly in the highlights

params.name: offset
params.does: Shifts shadows and midtones (-0.5..0.5): negative crushes blacks, positive lifts them to a faded grey

params.name: gammaCorrection
params.does: Simple power curve on the midtones (0.01..9.99, default 1.00); black and white points stay put

params.name: presetKind
params.does: Custom for your own values; Factory presets Plus 1.0, Plus 2.0, Minus 1.0, Minus 2.0

pairs_with: Curves to recover contrast after a big exposure lift
Vibrance to restore colour in brightened areas
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("presetKind"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindType"), stringIDToTypeID("presetKindCustom")); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("exposure"), 1.5); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("offset"), -0.05); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("gammaCorrection"), 1.0); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("exposure"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Exposure (adjustmentLayer:exposure)

verified.note: Same frame as the adjustment layer at the same values: strong brightening with the light half of the ramp and the wall blown to white.

cards.name: Gradient Map
cards.summary: Replaces every pixel's lightness with a colour from a gradient: the darkest tones take the left stop, the brightest the right stop, so a two-colour gradient gives a duotone poster look and a multi-stop gradient gives false colour or toning. The default gradient is Foreground to Background, so the result depends on the current colours unless the gradient is passed.
use_for: duotone posters and social graphics in brand colours
sepia, selenium and platinum toning with the Photographic Toning gradients (Sepia 1-5, Selenium 1-2, Platinum ...: load the Legacy Gradients set, Required/Legacy Gradients.grd)
high-contrast black-and-white via a black-to-white gradient with dither
false-colour / heat-map style artwork
avoid: leaving the gradient at the default: Foreground to Background takes whatever colours are set (the harvest session read green to black), so always pass the gradient in scripts
the gradient is an object the demo spec cannot carry: the gallery demo sets only the method / dither and keeps the app's current Foreground to Background
keeping natural skin or product colour: it discards all original hue
a non-destructive edit: use Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Gradient Map
needs a pixel layer: unavailable on a Smart Object or type layer

params.name: gradient
params.does: The gradient (gradientClassEvent): colour stops at location 0..4096 plus transparency stops; left = shadows, right = highlights
params.typical: two stops in brand colours, e.g. deep navy #1B2A6B to orange #FF8A3D

params.name: gradientsInterpolationMethod
params.does: How colours blend between stops: Classic, Linear, Perceptual, Smooth, or Stripes (the harvest lists it; its look is not verified here)

params.name: reverse
params.does: Flips the gradient: shadows take the right stop, highlights the left (a negative-style map)

params.name: dither
params.does: Adds slight noise to hide banding in smooth tones

pairs_with: Curves or Levels first to set where tones fall on the gradient
blend mode Color or Soft Light on the adjustment layer for a subtler tint
cards.scripting: function stop(r, g, b, loc) { var c = new ActionDescriptor(), s = new ActionDescriptor(); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("red"), r); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("grain"), g); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("blue"), b); s.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("color"), stringIDToTypeID("RGBColor"), c); s.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("type"), stringIDToTypeID("colorStopType"), stringIDToTypeID("userStop")); s.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("location"), loc); s.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("midpoint"), 50); return s; } var gr = new ActionDescriptor(); gr.putString(stringIDToTypeID("name"), "Custom"); gr.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("gradientForm"), stringIDToTypeID("gradientForm"), stringIDToTypeID("customStops")); gr.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("interfaceIconFrameDimmed"), 4096); var cl = new ActionList(); cl.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("colorStop"), stop(27, 42, 107, 0)); cl.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("colorStop"), stop(255, 138, 61, 4096)); gr.putList(stringIDToTypeID("colors"), cl); var tl = new ActionList(); for (var i = 0; i < 2; i++) { var t = new ActionDescriptor(); t.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("opacity"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 100); t.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("location"), i * 4096); t.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("midpoint"), 50); tl.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("transferSpec"), t); } gr.putList(stringIDToTypeID("transparency"), tl); var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("gradient"), stringIDToTypeID("gradientClassEvent"), gr); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("gradientsInterpolationMethod"), stringIDToTypeID("gradientInterpolationMethodType"), stringIDToTypeID("perceptual")); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("reverse"), false); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("dither"), true); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("gradientMapEvent"), d, DialogModes.NO); /* gradient layout = the harvested read-back */
cards.non_destructive: no: Image > Adjustments rewrites the layer's pixels (harvest extra.destructive = true) and is not a smart filter; the editable, maskable version is Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Gradient Map (adjustmentLayer:gradientMapClass)

review.changes: use_for: the Photographic Toning gradients are only in the Legacy Gradients set (harvested path Required/Legacy Gradients.grd/Legacy Gradients/Photographic Toning), not the default gradients; named them

verified.note: Black-to-white gradient map (default colours): the plate becomes black and white with darker Perceptual mid greys; the dropped "reverse" key is false, the default, so the frame is unaffected.
